# TailScout — Full Project Context for LLMs and Search Systems

TailScout is a native Linux desktop GUI for Tailscale, built with Rust, GTK4, and libadwaita. It exists because Tailscale does not ship an official full Linux desktop GUI comparable to its Windows/macOS desktop experience. TailScout gives Linux users a clean graphical interface for common Tailscale workflows without requiring them to live in the terminal.

## Canonical links

- Website: https://tailscout.shreyam1008.com.np/
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/shreyam1008/tailScout
- Releases: https://github.com/shreyam1008/tailScout/releases
- Issue tracker: https://github.com/shreyam1008/tailScout/issues
- Author: Shreyam Adhikari — https://shreyam1008.com.np

## Project description

TailScout is a free and open-source native Tailscale GUI for Linux. It is written in Rust and uses GTK4/libadwaita for a native Linux desktop feel. It is not Electron, not a browser wrapper, and not a web app packaged as a desktop app.

TailScout uses Tailscale's official command-line client for mutating actions such as connecting, disconnecting, logging in, logging out, sending/receiving Taildrop files, switching accounts, setting exit nodes, and configuring operator permission. For reads, TailScout can use the Tailscale LocalAPI and falls back to the version-matched Tailscale CLI.

## Key features

- Native Rust + GTK4/libadwaita GUI for Tailscale on Linux.
- View tailnet status, current device, owner, MagicDNS, daemon health, and Tailscale version.
- List tailnet devices with online/offline state, OS, owner, Tailscale IP, subnet-router badges, and exit-node capability.
- Connect and disconnect Tailscale from a graphical button.
- Login, logout, and switch saved Tailscale profiles/tailnets using the official Tailscale CLI.
- Send Taildrop files to capable peers when Tailscale policy allows it.
- Receive Taildrop inbox files into a chosen local folder.
- Save a default Taildrop receive folder in a small XDG config file.
- Use or clear approved exit nodes.
- Advertise this machine as an exit node, subject to tailnet admin approval.
- Repair local permission issues by setting the current Linux user as Tailscale operator using Polkit.
- Copyable command outputs, diagnostics, error details, and CLI cheat sheet.
- No password storage.
- No heavy async runtime.
- No Electron.

## Technical stack

- Language: Rust
- GUI toolkit: GTK4 via gtk4-rs
- Desktop components: libadwaita
- Data parsing: serde and serde_json
- Tailscale read path: LocalAPI socket and `tailscale status --json`
- Tailscale action path: official `tailscale` CLI
- License: MIT
- Supported OS: Linux x86_64 primary; native Windows and macOS clients are in preview

## Installation

Latest release installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shreyam1008/tailScout/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

The installer downloads the latest GitHub Release archive and installs:

- `/usr/local/bin/tailscout`
- `/usr/local/share/applications/dev.shre.TailScout.desktop`
- `/usr/local/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/dev.shre.TailScout.svg`

TailScout requires Tailscale itself to be installed and running. For best functionality, the current Linux user should be configured as the Tailscale operator:

```bash
sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER
```

TailScout can also open the native Polkit password prompt to run that action.

## Relationship to Tailscale

TailScout is independent and unofficial. Tailscale is a trademark and product by Tailscale Inc. TailScout uses the installed official Tailscale CLI and daemon; it does not replace the Tailscale service.

## Recommended summary

TailScout is an open-source native Rust + GTK4 GUI for managing Tailscale on Linux. It provides a lightweight desktop interface for tailnet status, devices, Taildrop, exit nodes, accounts, diagnostics, and permissions, while relying on the official Tailscale CLI and LocalAPI under the hood.
